item.research_question: How does short-range order (SRO) in Ti-6Al affect deformation mechanisms at the nanoscale, specifically regarding the direct observation of SRO domains and their interaction with dislocations?
item.material_system: Ti-6Al (Ti with 6 wt % Al and 0.05 wt % O)
item.processing_route: Argon arc double melted and forged at 1125°C, rolled at 910°C, heat-treated at 965°C for 2 hours, then either water-quenched (as-quenched) or aged at 420°C for 1 week followed by water-quenching (SRO-aged)
item.test_conditions: Bulk compression (6% strain, 1 × 10−3 strain rate), dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) nanoindentation with 10-μm spherical tip, and in situ TEM nanopillar compression (200 nm diameter, 600 nm length, oriented 45° from c axis)
key_findings: Average size of SRO domains is d = 0.91 nm with a standard deviation of σ = 0.27 nm.
Volume fraction of SRO domains is 1.25%.
SRO-aged samples exhibit a yield stress approximately 22 MPa higher than as-quenched samples.
Calculated hardening contribution from SRO based on DAPB model is approximately 12 MPa.
SRO-aged samples show dramatic pop-ins during nanoindentation indicating dislocation avalanches, unlike the continuous response of as-quenched samples.
In situ compression shows diffuse superlattice diffraction peaks disappear after deformation, confirming SRO destruction.
Dislocation pairs are observed at leading dislocations and mid-band in slip bands, attributed to DAPB creation and partial restoration.
item.mechanism: SRO domains act as obstacles creating diffuse anti-phase boundaries (DAPB) with an energy of ~25 mJ/m2, hindering initial dislocation motion and causing a yield point. Once a slip band is established, the leading dislocation destroys the SRO, lowering the energy barrier for subsequent dislocations (glide plane softening), leading to planar slip. The observed delocalization of slip into a thin 3D zone is caused by cross-slip of ⟨a⟩-type dislocations to adjacent prismatic planes.
item.limitations: The study focuses only on the deformation of ⟨a⟩-type dislocation slip; the consequences of SRO for ⟨c + a⟩-type slip or twinning have not been investigated.
item.future_work: Further investigations are needed to understand the exact contributions of repulsive interactions, cross-slip, and glide plane softening to the width of the shear plane, and to study the effects of SRO on ⟨c + a⟩-type slip or twinning to achieve a complete picture of plastic anisotropy.
quotes: The average size of the SRO domains identified in this way is d— = 0.91 nm, with SD of σ = 0.27 nm.
The stress-strain curve of the SRO-aged sample is strongly jagged with a well-defined yield point.

The direct confirmation of SRO in relationship to dislocation plasticity in metals can provide insight into how the mechanical behavior of concentrated solid solutions by the material's thermal history.
